You jest, but I have seen things like chocolate, peppercorns or cane sugar advertised as gluten-free.

I think they were even certified as such. Insanity.

In fairness, given the often unwholesome tendency of processed foods-producers to put various cheap ingredients into food products you'd least expect them in, it's probably a good thing to get clear assurances that product X doesn't contain potentially undesirable ingredient Y.

Please tell me when you've ever seen any grain product added to a pack of sugar. Or peppercorns. Even for chocolate, it's a bit of a stretch. I don't recall ever seeing anything more grain-like than rice-crispies in chocolate.

At the very least, I've seen chocolate that contained biscuit, which prolly contained gluten.

I would not put it past a US food producer to bulk up their (high import tariff) real sugar product with breadcrumbs or similar. Then again, there's surprisingly little I would categorically put past the unregulated/regulatory capture processed food industry.
I've seen corn starch put onto items to avoid them sticking together. Corn starch may or may not include gluten, so it's not that ridiculous.
Hard candies labeled as "fat free" makes me laugh.

Although I think the gluten fad has gotten really out of hand, a heavy reliance on grain does not do the body good. Grain is wonderful, especially for ancient man. It stores well, it last a while in your body, and it makes a meal a lot more satiating. It has classically been used to stretch a meal out and only the poorest in history have eaten a mostly grain diet.

Our food production makes foods that no longer resemble what they once were. We strip the hulls off grain and grind it where it releases oils that spoil within a few days. These flours sit for months or years before they are used. We all know whole grains are healthier for us, but almost every vegetable has a higher amount of fiber, vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants per calorie. We should seek to fill our plates with more fruits and vegetables with just a small portion of grains and meat.

I won't get into a whole thing on meat, but our mass produced (in the USA at least) meat is grade A dog shit. If the animal it comes from has to be on a steady regiment of anti-biotics it is not a healthy product. So most factory farmed meats should be minimized or eliminated from the diet as well.

In closing, all food is good for you - there is no new diet that will make you a healthier human than our ancestors. But we have removed so many factors that lead ancient man to have a good diet (mostly choice on what is in season) that we have to put the pieces back together again to make sense of what a good diet is.

The same goes for the anti-MSG craze. I've never spoken to a single person who avoids MSG and also knows what MSG is. Which is a good representation of our critical thinking skills in our society.

And of course, when you calmly explain that MSG is just a sodium ion and an amino acid your body produces on its own, these words mean nothing to them, and does nothing to alter their opinion.
It doesn't matter how harmless it is. I avoid MSG anyway because it makes me sleepy and messes up the rest of my day.
that's not the MSG that causes that.
Interesting. I just found that it may be the carbs. I never really thought about it because avoiding Chinese food has worked so well in the past. Thanks.

:P Anything that has a lot of fat or starches can cause sleepiness. Basically everything you eat has MSG in it in some form or another, even if it's not listed on the nutrition label. Even salad. In every cell of the lettuce has sodium ions, and what little protein is in the cells is partially made up of the amino acid glutamate, which is broken down and released into the digestive system.

The way MSG became a nasty word today is pretty funny.. Once upon a time, a scientist went to a Chinese restaurant, and became sick that night. He was furious, and put the blame squarely on MSG for some reason. But in reality it's no worse for you than table salt.
